headline: Sales return to growth, margins expand, guidance raised
summary_short: Net sales rose 3.0% y/y to $1,994M (core sales +2.3%) as gross margin expanded to 40.7% from 35.4% and operating margin to 14.2% from 8.8%; diluted EPS was $0.25 versus $0.11, aided by roughly $126M of IEEPA tariff recoveries, and the company raised its full-year 2026 outlook.
summary_long: Net sales grew 3.0% y/y to $1,994M on 2.3% core sales growth plus favorable foreign exchange, with Learning & Development leading (+4.9% core). Gross margin rose to 40.7% from 35.4%, helped by roughly $126M of IEEPA tariff recoveries and productivity savings, partly offset by inflation. Operating margin improved to 14.2% from 8.8% as higher gross profit outweighed increased advertising spend. Diluted EPS was $0.25 versus $0.11 (normalized $0.42 vs $0.24). Cash was $209M and long-term debt $4,536M, both roughly flat y/y; H1 operating cash outflow narrowed to $204M from $271M. The company raised FY2026 guidance across sales, margin, EPS, and cash flow, and initiated Q3 2026 guidance.

drivers.explanation: Sales returned to y/y growth for the first time in over four years on stronger innovation, higher advertising support, and improved go-to-market execution, plus roughly $126M of IEEPA tariff recoveries; results beat management's own expectations, prompting a raised full-year outlook.

Net sales rose 3.0% on 2.3% core sales growth and favorable foreign exchange; Learning & Development (core +4.9%) and Outdoor & Recreation (core +3.7%) grew while Home & Commercial Solutions core sales fell 0.4%.
Cost of products sold fell as a share of sales as gross margin benefited from tariff recoveries and gross productivity savings, partly offset by higher inflation costs.
Gross margin expanded to 40.7% from 35.4%, mainly from about $126M of IEEPA tariff recoveries and gross productivity savings, partially offset by higher inflation costs.
Operating income rose as higher gross profit was only partly offset by higher advertising and promotion spending; normalized operating margin improved to 16.2% from 10.7%.
Pretax income rose in step with the operating-income gain; net interest expense ticked up to $87M from $82M and the prior year included a $13M debt-extinguishment loss not repeated this quarter.
Net income rose with pretax income, though a higher effective tax rate (45.6% vs 35.2% a year ago) partly offset the gain; normalized net income rose to $180M from $101M.
EPS rose in line with net income growth; diluted share count was up only 2.2% y/y, so per-share gains tracked closely with the net income increase.
Diluted EPS moved with net income; normalized diluted EPS of $0.42 (vs $0.24) also reflects roughly $0.17/share of IEEPA tariff recoveries booked this quarter.
Cash fell to $209M from $219M y/y; the tariff recovery had not yet been collected as of quarter-end, and the company still expects the cash refund in the second half.

Long-term debt was little changed at $4,536M versus $4,535M a year ago; subsequent to quarter-end the company entered a new $800M asset-based revolving credit facility maturing 2031, replacing the prior revolver.
